viral dsRNA induces a MyD88 and/or TRIF-dependent inflammatory response and antiviral state, while viral ssRNA induces a more potent inflammatory response and ant-viral state that is MyD88 and/ or TRIF dependent.
dsRNA induces a more restricted cytokine profile in the FM, whereas ssRNA induces a broader panel of inflammatory mediators in the FM, which is mediated through different signaling pathways.
dsRNA and ssRNA are different in their ability to induce cytokine production and antiviral gene expression in FMs.
